title: Improve shell guidance for Windows hosts

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue is a clear, actionable bug report requesting platform-aware shell guidance in system prompts on Windows hosts, preferring commands like findstr, Get-Content -Tail, and Select-String.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The change involves updating prompt generation options and templates in packages/core/src/prompts/snippets.ts and packages/core/src/prompts/promptProvider.ts to conditionally format Windows-specific commands, alongside updating unit tests in packages/core/src/core/prompts.test.ts.

summary.problem: System prompt shell-efficiency guidance is not platform-aware for Windows hosts, leading agents to suggest Unix-centric commands instead of Windows-native alternatives.
summary.root_cause: In packages/core/src/prompts/snippets.ts, OperationalGuidelinesOptions and renderOperationalGuidelines lack platform-specific shell efficiency instructions for process.platform === 'win32'.
summary.context: Related to PR #27603. Inspecting large command output on Windows should prefer targeted Windows/PowerShell commands such as findstr, Get-Content -Tail, and Select-String over full-output dumps or Unix tools.

steps: Update OperationalGuidelinesOptions in packages/core/src/prompts/snippets.ts to include enableShellEfficiency?: boolean.
In packages/core/src/prompts/snippets.ts, update renderOperationalGuidelines to include shell efficiency guidelines when enabled.
Condition the shell efficiency command examples on process.platform === 'win32' to recommend findstr, Get-Content -Tail, and Select-String on Windows hosts.
Ensure packages/core/src/prompts/promptProvider.ts correctly passes enableShellEfficiency into operationalGuidelines options in getCoreSystemPrompt.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: System prompt generation on win32 includes recommendations for findstr, Get-Content -Tail, and Select-String, while non-Windows platforms receive Unix shell guidance.
verification_steps: Run unit tests using Vitest in packages/core/src/core/prompts.test.ts.
Verify that mocking process.platform to win32 includes findstr, Get-Content -Tail, and Select-String in the operational guidelines prompt.
Verify that non-Windows platform execution renders standard Unix command guidance.
